blocks.heading: Types of business activity
blocks.text: The five basic activity types are primary, manufacturing, wholesale, retail and service. They describe what a business does, rather than its legal ownership. Primary activity extracts or obtains natural resources. Manufacturing changes materials into products. Wholesaling buys goods in bulk and supplies other businesses; retailing supplies final consumers. Service activity provides an activity, skill or assistance rather than principally transferring ownership of a physical product.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented grower supplies grain, a mill processes it, and Omuti Foods makes bread for households. The grower’s activity is primary. Milling grain and making bread involve manufacturing. A distributor buying large consignments for shops is a wholesaler; a shop selling loaves to households is a retailer. A vehicle-repair workshop supporting deliveries supplies a service. One enterprise can carry out more than one activity, so classification should identify the particular operation being described.

blocks.heading: A primary business
blocks.text: A primary business obtains natural resources, such as agricultural produce or fish. Its activity supplies inputs that other businesses may process.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented grower harvests grain near a Namibian town. Growing the grain is primary activity; milling it later would be a separate manufacturing stage.

blocks.heading: A manufacturing business
blocks.text: A manufacturing business transforms materials into products. It may produce finished goods or inputs that another manufacturer will process further.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented workshop turns timber into school desks. The transformation of timber into desks is manufacturing, irrespective of who owns the workshop.

blocks.heading: A wholesaler
blocks.text: A wholesaler buys goods in relatively large quantities and resells to other businesses, often in smaller quantities. The buyer’s business use distinguishes this role from retailing.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented distributor buys cartons of soap and supplies independent shops. Its customers are shops that will resell the soap, so the distributor is operating as a wholesaler.

blocks.heading: A retailer
blocks.text: A retailer sells goods to final consumers for their own use. It may provide convenience through location, smaller quantities and a range of products.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented shop sells one packet of flour to a household. The household is the final consumer, so this sale is retailing rather than wholesaling.

blocks.heading: A service business
blocks.text: A service business provides an activity, skill or assistance to customers or other businesses. Its principal offer may be transport, repair, advice or personal care.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented mechanic repairs a bakery’s delivery vehicle. The repair is a service that helps the bakery operate; it is not the manufacture of a new vehicle.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why calling an invented furniture maker a partnership does not identify its activity type.

Partnership describes an ownership arrangement, while manufacturing describes transforming materials into furniture. Two partners can own a manufacturer, retailer or service firm. In this case, what happens to the timber identifies manufacturing; the number of owners does not. The categories can both be stated without treating them as alternatives.
